fix(panel): divide the requested width once, so no row can overflow it (rich-width-3cf.1) (#76)

* fix(panel): divide the requested width once, so no row can overflow it (rich-width-3cf.1)

`Panel` derived its geometry three times — `panelWidth - 2 - padLeft -
padRight` in `render`, `panelWidth - 2` in each border renderer — and
clamped each derivation differently. At width 1 the unclamped border
subtraction went negative and `String.repeat(-1)` threw `RangeError`.
Between widths 2 and 6 the `Math.max(1, …)` in `render` clamped the
content canvas *up*, so a 2-cell frame enclosed 5-cell content rows,
which the terminal then soft-wrapped, destroying the frame of everything
printed below.

`layoutPanel` now divides the requested width once into fields that sum
to exactly that width, and every row measures from it. Cells go to the
two frame columns, then one cell of content, then the padding, then the
remainder back to content — so content stays visible down to width 3
instead of the panel spending its last cells on padding. Frame columns
are emitted as `box.left.repeat(n)` with n in {0,1}, which needs no
branch because the wire boundary drops zero-length segments.

Content rows now route through `Segment.adjustLineLength`, which crops a
child that rendered wider than its canvas (a `Table` at natural width)
instead of letting it burst the frame, and fills the span in one stroke
— replacing the hand-rolled `rightPad` arithmetic and `_renderBlankLine`,
which is now a content row whose content is nothing.

The test sweeps thirteen panel configurations across widths 1–40 and
asserts every line fits inside the width and no line is ragged.

* fix(panel): keep rendering content at widths that cannot show it

`_renderContent` skipped the wrapped renderable entirely when the canvas
was zero cells, which silently broke the contract the `BorderAccessory`
doc states two dozen lines above it: the thunk form is evaluated after
content has rendered for the current frame, because it reads state that
render populates. At panel width 2 and below the thunk still fired and
read the previous frame.

Content now renders at every width and the geometry decides how many of
its rows survive, so only the row count varies. The nominal width of 1
is a floor `RichText` needs rather than a clamp: its fold walks a cursor
forward by `maxWidth`, so a zero-width canvas spins ~134M iterations and
about a gigabyte before `push` hits the array-length limit — measured,
not inferred. Fixing that loop would delete this floor, but what fold
should emit into a zero-column canvas is a decision for every RichText
caller and belongs with the width sweep in rich-width-3cf.3.

The test asserts the contract where it is observable: an accessory thunk
reading a counter its content renderable increments, at every width from
1 up. It fails against the previous commit at width 1.

* fix(padding): floor padding at zero where it is parsed, once

Negative padding reached the renderers, which handled it three ways:
`Panel` on master drew a 21-cell content row inside a 20-cell border,
`Table` drew a 6-cell row inside a 5-cell border or threw `RangeError:
Invalid count value` depending on how wide the column was, and the
`layoutPanel` geometry introduced by this branch turned the panel case
from silent corruption into a throw. All three are the same defect: the
public `PaddingDimensions` vocabulary admits a value no renderer can
draw.

`normalizePadding` is the crossing between that vocabulary and the
four-sided tuple every renderable indexes by, so the floor goes there
and `" ".repeat(left)` downstream needs no guard in any renderable.

It also existed three times — `padding.ts`, `panel.ts` and `table.ts`,
the latter two byte-identical — so clamping one copy would have left the
bug in the others. There is now one exported parser beside the type it
parses, and the per-renderable defaults stay at their callsites, since
those genuinely differ.

Both tests were checked against the unfixed code. The Table one earns
its keep twice: written first as `not.toThrow`, it passed on master's
corrupt output, because that input draws a ragged table rather than
throwing. Asserting the table is a rectangle catches both shapes.

* fix(panel): measure against the same division the panel renders against

`measure()` and `_getPanelWidth()` still derived the content budget as
`Math.max(1, maxWidth - 2 - padLeft - padRight)`. Before `layoutPanel`
existed that formula was textually identical to the one in `render`, so
the two could not disagree; introducing the geometry made them two
sources for one fact that diverge exactly in the 0-2 band this branch
was written for — the geometry gives 0 content cells there, the formula
insists on 1. The comment on `PanelGeometry` claiming one authoritative
division was written eight lines above the code contradicting it.

Both now read the geometry. Taking the frame overhead from it as well,
rather than the constant `2 + padLeft + padRight`, fixes a second
incoherence with the same cause — a panel does not spend cells on a
right frame column or padding it cannot afford, so counting them
produced a measurement whose minimum exceeded its own maximum:

  before: @1 {minimum: 5, maximum: 1}   after: @1 {1, 1}
          @2 {minimum: 5, maximum: 2}           @2 {2, 2}
          @20 {minimum: 9, maximum: 15}         @20 {9, 15}

The negative-padding tests asserted the rendered lines were rectangular,
which `layoutPanel` guarantees for any non-negative clamp — they would
have passed had the floor been `Math.abs`. They now compare against the
`padding: 0` render, which is the claim their names make. Verified by
mutating the clamp to `Math.abs` and watching both fail.
